To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
highly allosensitized human patients awaiting renal allotransplant are at no increased risk for xenoreactivity against GalT-KOs compared to non-sensitized patients.

1) highly allosensitized sera from patients on transplant waiting lists have no increased risk of reactivity against GalT-K0 miniature swine; 2) the majority of anti-GalT-knockout swine reactivity is mediated by preformed anti-Gal antibodies; and 3 ) the degree of allosensitization is not predictive of the degree of reactivity against xenogeneic GalT-knockout cells.
highly sensitized transplant patients do not have an increased risk of xenoreactivity to α-1,3-Galatcosyltransferase knockout miniature swine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel immunomodulatory therapy for the treatment of acute and chronic rejection of human renal allografts.
the identification and development of novel strategies to improve the outcome of solid organ and stem cell transplantation in patients with end stage organ failure.
the development of novel therapies for the treatment of patients with acute kidney injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
allosensitized recipients of human organs are not at increased risk of xenoreactivity to GalT-KO pigs.
allosensitized recipients of renal allografts do not appear to have an increased risk of xenoreactivity to GalT-KO pig tissues.
highly allosensitized renal transplant patients do not seem to have an increased risk of sensitization against SLA antigens expressed by α1,3 galactosyltransferse gene knocked out miniature swine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
highly allosensitized individuals are at no increased risk to develop xenosensitizations to GalT-KO pigs.

the risk of xenosensitivity in highly sensitized patients is no higher than that in the general population, and that the majority of xenoreactivity is mediated by preformed anti-GalT IgM antibodies, which can be removed by DTT treatment.
allosensitization does not increase the risk of xenoreactivity to GalT-KO mini pigs in patients on transplantation waiting lists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
highly-allosensitized individuals awaiting kidney transplants are at no greater risk for sensitizing to GalT-KO pig organs than non-sensitized individuals.
the risk of xenoreactivity to GalT-KO pigs in highly allosensitized renal transplant candidates is no higher than in non-allosensitized candidates.
the GalT-KO pig is a very good xenograft for highly allosensitized human recipients.
